request.system:
You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

VERIFICATION TRIAGE INVARIANT (mandatory)
When verification capacity is limited, prioritize inherited beliefs that are both highly consequential to the current decision and insufficiently supported for the objective being optimized.
request.user:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation. Fewer required fields at
    signup produced a durable lift.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; a
    demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB
    segments — strong acquisition and revenue lift.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers and added
    qualified revenue without hurting retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shorter onboarding improved time-to-value and completion rates.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging improved week-one engagement.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

first.rationale: Triage logic: the two inherited beliefs that are both most consequential this week and least supported for the stated objective (sustainable long-term QUALIFIED revenue) are memory_73 and memory_31. memory_73 is the memory the competitive situation most strongly pulls toward, and its recorded evidence is acquisition/revenue lift — metrics that are typically short-horizon and silent on discount-cohort retention, margin, and expansion. If that record turns out to be a short-window acquisition test, promotional pricing is the highest-regret choice available, since it also risks anchoring price against a competitor whose entry pricing we cannot profitably match. memory_31 is the belief underwriting my intended action, and 'fewer required fields' is exactly the kind of change that can lift a funnel metric while degrading downstream qualification: fewer fields means less firmographic data for routing and scoring, which could quietly suppress the enterprise sales-assisted path that memory_44 says produces the best pipeline quality. So I want the original record to confirm whether the 'durable lift' was measured on activation only or followed through to qualified revenue. I am not verifying memory_57 (its record already claims a retention-neutral, qualified-revenue-positive result, so it is comparatively well-supported), memory_86/memory_91 (directionally consistent with memory_31 and individually lower-stakes), or memory_44 (not the action I intend). Intended action: simplify_onboarding, because it is the one direction that addresses both observed internal declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) at their shared root rather than buying volume, and because onboarding/time-to-value gains tend to compound into retention rather than trade against it. Run it as a small guarded test with explicit stop conditions on downstream value: halt if lead-qualification completeness, enterprise demo-request rate, or trial-to-paid quality degrades, not merely if completion rate rises. Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose measurement horizons are unstated, the two QoQ declines may be competitor-driven demand-mix shifts rather than funnel defects (in which case an onboarding fix will underperform), and if the memory_31 archive shows the lift was activation-only with no revenue follow-through I will downgrade to activation_messaging rather than expand this test.

final.rationale: The archive resolved both questions in a way that sharpens rather than reverses my plan. exp_73 vindicates the triage: promotional pricing's headline (+31% signup, +18% qualified revenue) is real but 30-day retention is -12%, and the source record's own conclusion explicitly forbids generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The acquired cohort does not survive first renewal, so under a primary objective of SUSTAINABLE long-term qualified revenue, promotional_pricing is now affirmatively ruled out, not merely deprioritized — matching the competitor's entry pricing would buy a cohort that churns before it pays back. This is the single most valuable thing the budget bought, since the competitive pressure was pulling hard toward exactly that mistake. exp_31 confirms my intended action on the merits: signup +15%, activation +9%, retention -1%, and critically qualified revenue +4% — the follow-through to downstream value I was worried might be absent. So the lift is not a funnel-metric artifact. Two caveats survive verification and shape the design. First, exp_31 'holds on SMB; not replicated on other segments,' so I scope this to the SMB self-serve funnel only and make no claim about enterprise; this also structurally protects the memory_44 sales-assisted path, since I am not touching enterprise routing or the demo-request flow and therefore not stripping the firmographic fields that qualification depends on. Second, the -1% retention is small but non-zero and directionally the same sign as the discounting failure mode, so I keep downstream-value risk flagged and instrument accordingly. Guardrails: primary readout is qualified revenue and 30-day retention, not completion rate; stop if retention degrades beyond roughly the -1% precedent, if lead-qualification completeness or enterprise demo-request rate moves at all, or if activation gains fail to carry into trial-to-paid quality. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout because the evidence is confirmed for precisely this intervention and segment but unreplicated elsewhere; standard rather than minimal because I no longer need the verification-stage caution about whether the effect reaches revenue at all. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving this week: the -6% activation and -4% onboarding declines may be competitor-driven demand-mix shifts rather than funnel defects, in which case this test will underperform its exp_31 baseline; that outcome would be evidence about demand composition, not a refutation of memory_31. If the test disappoints, the next slot goes to activation_messaging (memory_91) or a defensibility play on established customers via memory_57, never to discounting.
